entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating a single laboratory task or response-time difference as a pure measure of a broad cognitive construct.
entities.definition: The degree to which a represented stimulus or feature stands out and attracts priority in attention.
entities.evidenceNotes: Scientifically defensible with substantial supporting literature, while causal identification, construct boundaries, measurement, or transferability remain context dependent. Representative records: SRC148; SRC125.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Cognitive tasks; eye tracking or attention probes; workload scales; response-time and accuracy measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Task measures often have low cross-task reliability and can reflect strategy, motivation, speed-accuracy tradeoffs, or sensory limits.
entities.mechanism: Raises the probability and speed of attention and increases the weight of associated information.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Expertise, task complexity, time pressure, fatigue, motivation, modality, and environmental distraction.
entities.name: Attentional Salience
entities.persistenceRecovery: Usually task-bound and rapidly reversible, although learning and fatigue can produce longer effects.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater psychological prominence and capture priority.
entities.representationScale: Low–high subjective salience; attentional capture index

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating a single laboratory task or response-time difference as a pure measure of a broad cognitive construct.
entities.definition: The capacity currently available to shift perspectives, rules, or strategies in response to changing demands.
entities.evidenceNotes: Scientifically defensible with substantial supporting literature, while causal identification, construct boundaries, measurement, or transferability remain context dependent. Representative records: SRC150; SRC149.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Cognitive tasks; eye tracking or attention probes; workload scales; response-time and accuracy measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Task measures often have low cross-task reliability and can reflect strategy, motivation, speed-accuracy tradeoffs, or sensory limits.
entities.mechanism: Supports updating, perspective change, and strategy switching when the environment changes.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Expertise, task complexity, time pressure, fatigue, motivation, modality, and environmental distraction.
entities.name: Cognitive Flexibility
entities.persistenceRecovery: Momentary deployment recovers with rest or context change; trained capacity may persist longer.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater ability to adapt cognitive set or strategy.
entities.representationScale: Low–high flexibility; switch cost; validated flexibility measure

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating a single laboratory task or response-time difference as a pure measure of a broad cognitive construct.
entities.definition: The amount of limited cognitive-processing capacity currently occupied by task demands and concurrent mental operations.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC149; SRC147.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Cognitive tasks; eye tracking or attention probes; workload scales; response-time and accuracy measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Task measures often have low cross-task reliability and can reflect strategy, motivation, speed-accuracy tradeoffs, or sensory limits.
entities.mechanism: Reduces resources available for elaboration, working memory, inhibition, and complex choice.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Expertise, task complexity, time pressure, fatigue, motivation, modality, and environmental distraction.
entities.name: Cognitive Load
entities.persistenceRecovery: Usually task-bound and rapidly reversible, although learning and fatigue can produce longer effects.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = more occupied cognitive capacity.
entities.representationScale: Low–high workload; task-load manipulation; performance-derived estimate

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating a single laboratory task or response-time difference as a pure measure of a broad cognitive construct.
entities.definition: The currently active representation that organizes which aspects, comparisons, or meanings of a situation are foregrounded.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC113; SRC183.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Cognitive tasks; eye tracking or attention probes; workload scales; response-time and accuracy measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Task measures often have low cross-task reliability and can reflect strategy, motivation, speed-accuracy tradeoffs, or sensory limits.
entities.mechanism: Changes which attributes and reference comparisons enter appraisal and valuation.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Expertise, task complexity, time pressure, fatigue, motivation, modality, and environmental distraction.
entities.name: Construal Frame
entities.persistenceRecovery: Usually task-bound and rapidly reversible, although learning and fatigue can produce longer effects.
entities.polarityDirection: Categories identify alternative construals and have no inherent universal ordering.
entities.representationScale: Frame category; gain/loss; concrete/abstract; diagnostic coding

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating a single laboratory task or response-time difference as a pure measure of a broad cognitive construct.
entities.definition: The degree of effortful, issue-relevant cognitive processing applied to information or a decision.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC117; SRC162.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Cognitive tasks; eye tracking or attention probes; workload scales; response-time and accuracy measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Task measures often have low cross-task reliability and can reflect strategy, motivation, speed-accuracy tradeoffs, or sensory limits.
entities.mechanism: Increases integration with prior knowledge and can produce more durable, confidence-linked judgments.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Expertise, task complexity, time pressure, fatigue, motivation, modality, and environmental distraction.
entities.name: Elaboration Depth
entities.persistenceRecovery: Usually task-bound and rapidly reversible, although learning and fatigue can produce longer effects.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = deeper and more effortful issue-relevant processing.
entities.representationScale: Low–high elaboration; thought count/quality; processing-time index

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating a single laboratory task or response-time difference as a pure measure of a broad cognitive construct.
entities.definition: The experienced ease with which a stimulus or thought is perceived, retrieved, or processed.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC125; SRC171.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Cognitive tasks; eye tracking or attention probes; workload scales; response-time and accuracy measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Task measures often have low cross-task reliability and can reflect strategy, motivation, speed-accuracy tradeoffs, or sensory limits.
entities.mechanism: Functions as a metacognitive cue that can affect familiarity, truth, confidence, liking, and effort allocation.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Expertise, task complexity, time pressure, fatigue, motivation, modality, and environmental distraction.
entities.name: Processing Fluency
entities.persistenceRecovery: Usually task-bound and rapidly reversible, although learning and fatigue can produce longer effects.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater subjective ease of processing.
entities.representationScale: Low–high ease rating; response latency or disfluency manipulation

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating a single laboratory task or response-time difference as a pure measure of a broad cognitive construct.
entities.definition: The proportion of available attention directed toward a specified stimulus, location, feature, or task.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC148; SRC109.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Cognitive tasks; eye tracking or attention probes; workload scales; response-time and accuracy measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Task measures often have low cross-task reliability and can reflect strategy, motivation, speed-accuracy tradeoffs, or sensory limits.
entities.mechanism: Changes which information is encoded, elaborated, and available for downstream appraisal and choice.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Expertise, task complexity, time pressure, fatigue, motivation, modality, and environmental distraction.
entities.name: Selective Attention Allocation
entities.persistenceRecovery: Usually task-bound and rapidly reversible, although learning and fatigue can produce longer effects.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater attention allocated to the specified target.
entities.representationScale: 0–1 share of attention; dwell time proportion; probe-based bias

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Treating a single laboratory task or response-time difference as a pure measure of a broad cognitive construct.
entities.definition: The amount of working-memory capacity currently available for maintaining and manipulating task-relevant information.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC147; SRC148; SRC149.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Cognitive tasks; eye tracking or attention probes; workload scales; response-time and accuracy measures
entities.measurementCaveats: Task measures often have low cross-task reliability and can reflect strategy, motivation, speed-accuracy tradeoffs, or sensory limits.
entities.mechanism: Supports integration, planning, inhibition, and resistance to distraction.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Expertise, task complexity, time pressure, fatigue, motivation, modality, and environmental distraction.
entities.name: Working Memory Availability
entities.persistenceRecovery: Usually task-bound and rapidly reversible, although learning and fatigue can produce longer effects.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = more capacity available for current processing.
entities.representationScale: Low–high available capacity; residual span/performance estimate
